PVLib Python is a Python library for modeling photovoltaic systems. It provides a wide range of functionalities for simulating solar radiation, weather conditions, and power generation.

## Installation

To install PVLib Python, you can use pip:

```bash
pip install pvlib
```

## Usage

PVLib Python provides several modules for different aspects of solar energy modeling. Here are some basic examples:

### Solar Radiation

PVLib Python includes a module called `solarposition` which calculates the position of the sun at any given location and time.

```python
import pvlib.solarposition

# Define the location
location = {
    'latitude': 34.052235,
    'longitude': -118.243724,
    'elevation': 0,
}

# Calculate the solar position
times = ['2023-04-01T12:00:00', '2023-04-01T13:00:00']
solar_position = pvlib.solarposition.get_solarposition(times, location)

print(solar_position)
```

### Weather Conditions

PVLib Python also includes a module called `weatherdata` which retrieves weather data from various sources.

```python
import pvlib.weatherdata

# Define the location
location = {
    'latitude': 34.052235,
    'longitude': -118.243724,
    'elevation': 0,
}

# Retrieve weather data
weather_data = pvlib.weatherdata.get_weather(location, times)

print(weather_data)
```

### Power Generation

PVLib Python provides a module called `powermodels` which models power generation based on various factors.

```python
import pvlib.powermodels

# Define the location
location = {
    'latitude': 34.052235,
    'longitude': -118.243724,
    'elevation': 0,
}

# Define the solar position
solar_position = pvlib.solarposition.get_solarposition(times, location)

# Define the weather data
weather_data = pvlib.weatherdata.get_weather(location, times)

# Model power generation
power_generation = pvlib.powermodels.compute_power_generation(solar_position, weather_data)

print(power_generation)
```

## Documentation

For more information and documentation, please visit the official PVLib Python website: https://pypi.org/project/pvlib/

## Contributing

Contributions to PVLib Python are welcome! Please read our contributing guidelines: https://github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

## License

PVLib Python is licensed under the MIT License. See LICENSE for details."}))

<pr_description>
Add Wavelet Variability Model (WVM) for calculating spatial smoothing of irradiance
> > Should I spin this off to a separate issue, since it might be different (and more compartmented) than the broader downscaling discussion?
> 
> Yes. Let's start a new module with this submission, `scaling.py` comes to mind, but I'm not enamored of it. Scope will be functions that operate on irradiance, perhaps other variables, to transform temporal or spatial characteristics.

Spinoff from [issue #788 ](https://github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python/issues/788). Implementation is a python port of WVM, released as an auxiliary to the Matlab pvlib [here](https://pvpmc.sandia.gov/applications/wavelet-variability-model/). My implementation ports the original model logic, but deviates from the overall package, in that I begin at the point where the user already has a clear sky index to operate on (original starts from GHI and calculates POA clear sky index). I thought this would allow for more flexibility in choice of transposition model, etc, but it does ask a bit more work up front for a user to run the WVM.

I am close to completion of a draft and will create a pull request when ready. This is my first contribution to the project (or any open source project really), so please accept my apologies in advance if it takes some guidance.

</pr_description>

instance.problem_statement:
Add Wavelet Variability Model (WVM) for calculating spatial smoothing of irradiance
> > Should I spin this off to a separate issue, since it might be different (and more compartmented) than the broader downscaling discussion?
> 
> Yes. Let's start a new module with this submission, `scaling.py` comes to mind, but I'm not enamored of it. Scope will be functions that operate on irradiance, perhaps other variables, to transform temporal or spatial characteristics.

Spinoff from [issue #788 ](https://github.com/pvlib/pvlib-python/issues/788). Implementation is a python port of WVM, released as an auxiliary to the Matlab pvlib [here](https://pvpmc.sandia.gov/applications/wavelet-variability-model/). My implementation ports the original model logic, but deviates from the overall package, in that I begin at the point where the user already has a clear sky index to operate on (original starts from GHI and calculates POA clear sky index). I thought this would allow for more flexibility in choice of transposition model, etc, but it does ask a bit more work up front for a user to run the WVM.

I am close to completion of a draft and will create a pull request when ready. This is my first contribution to the project (or any open source project really), so please accept my apologies in advance if it takes some guidance.
